title: Feature detection and graceful fallback
learningObjectives: Explain feature detection and graceful fallback and apply the visual effect with a usable fallback.

understand.concept: Feature detection checks whether a browser supports a CSS capability before applying an enhancement. @supports can test property/value support or selector support. A baseline style should remain usable when the enhancement is unavailable.
understand.whyItMatters: A support query does not guarantee that every use case works perfectly, nor does it detect user preference. Progressive enhancement keeps core content and interaction available before adding optional features.
understand.analogy: Feature detection is like checking whether a tool is available while keeping a basic tool ready.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual painting, clipping, and media behaviour follow CSS rendering rules.

explain.narrative: The baseline border and padding remain. Grid enhancement applies only where the browser reports support.

practise.guidedTask: Choose a modern CSS feature and add a baseline layout plus an @supports enhancement. Explain what remains when support is absent.
practise.independentTask: Create a decorative component using this effect. Test readability, responsive sizing, and a baseline appearance when the effect is unavailable.
hints: Keep important information in semantic HTML.
Test the effect on different sizes and backgrounds.
Do not let decorative effects obscure focus or text.

questions.explanation: @supports applies declarations conditionally based on reported CSS feature support.
